restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages m(a), m(b) of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 (zero state, rate 136, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5, full 256-bit digest). m(u) places the point u (lanes u0..u3) in lanes 1, 6, 11 = u0, u1, u0^u1^K11 and 4, 9, 14 = u2, u3, u2^u3^K14, the other lanes 0..15 fixed constants K (proof.md Section 2); m is injective. F(u) = digest of m(u) xor a fixed mask PD; F(a) = F(b) with a != b is an ordinary collision. Column sums of the message lanes are constant and no two are chi-adjacent, so round 0 and round-1 theta are affine in u (a Guo-Liu-Song 2016 linear structure).

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on F with 256 walks per step, as in our entry 2d74a370: DP = planes 142..255 zero (H = 114), cap 17 x 2^114 steps, at most 21,000 trails and a table of 21,000 words, Tb = 67878312 x 2^94 steps, a prefilter-hit counter that aborts the attempt at hit HMAX + 1 (HMAX = floor(Tb (1 + 2^-20)/2^8) + 1 + Lc), one replay with the selected-round permutation (proof.md Section 4).

One step of 256 walks is a generated bit-sliced straight line of 28,543 register operations (20,955 XOR, 3,985 AND, 2,671 OR, 932 NOT; no loads or stores): lazy per-row theta, per-row complement subsets, dead-code elimination, last-use allocation (step design after jungjipdo's 67f781f8, our own generator gen.c, Appendix B). Executed and compared with a plain six-round implementation: 2,048 chained evaluations, 0 mismatches (Section 3.7).

Cost model collision-frontier-v5, unit 1626: N = Tb x 28,563 + (2 x 1661 + 19) x Lc + R + PRE = 39623246885746059599222323362107280213464 word operations, every loop-control, test and handler operation counted, at most HMAX + 1 prefilter hits at 116 each in every execution, PRE = 513 x 2^32 + 512 x 2^10 for the selection run gen 512, replay at one unit per permutation call plus 35 (Section 4); time_log2 = 124.19636 = log2(N/1626) rounded up, integer certificate 1626^100000 2^12419635 < N^100000 <= 1626^100000 2^12419636 (Appendix A).

Declared heuristics H_reg and H_code (Section 3.5): H_reg, a file of 2,192 registers of 256 bits, its 70,144 bytes counted as memory, all transfers charged as stated; H_code, the straight line is native code stored at 5 bytes per instruction (opcode, three 12-bit register numbers), executed directly with no interpreter, so no decode or dispatch is executed or charged; other code at 32 bytes per instruction. Priced alternatives in Section 8 (1,024 registers 124.608, 256 registers 124.966, 32-byte code about 124.82).

Memory at most 1,042,630 bytes <= 2^20 (registers, code, table, walk state, scratch, constants; Section 6); the selection run gen 512 runs before the search (phases do not overlap) with a measured peak of at most 561,152 bytes (703,867 with its output), so memory_log2_bytes = 20 and the score is 124.19636. The declared Python experiments are reduced-width evidence, not the attack; their measured peaks (72 MB, 50 MB) are stated separately in Section 6.

Success at least 0.39 for one attempt over the fresh word rho, under the score-critical premise H_rand (F behaves as a random function on the evaluated points), with failure terms for cut trails, table limit, self-coincidence, starts and key matches, and the hit-counter abort F5 < 2^-1000, proved by a Chernoff bound (Section 5). Preprocessing: the constant-selection run gen 512 (512 candidate sets, the best rebuilt), charged 513 x 2^32 + 512 x 2^10 operations, preprocessing_log2 31. No advice. No full-scale run and no full collision is claimed.

heuristics.statement: F(u) = SHA3-256-r6(m(u)) xor PD, with the linear-structure message embedding m of proof.md Section 2, behaves as a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values on the points the search evaluates: values at distinct inputs are independent and uniform, a fresh point is a distinguished point with probability 2^-114, and the remaining length of a trail after a coincidence is geometric with parameter 2^-114 independently of the time of the coincidence. Then the first image coincidence among e evaluations has probability at least 1 - exp(-e(e-1)/2^257), and one attempt succeeds with probability at least 0.39 after the failure terms of proof.md Section 5.
heuristics.scope: The fixed function F of proof.md Section 2 on the points of one attempt: about 1.0115 x 2^128 evaluations in 256 lockstep walks from starts rho + i, i < 21,000. Only the pair-coincidence rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate enter the bound. Nothing else is assumed: the step program, the cost, the memory and the failure terms are derived.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-executed: rho-w22 runs the whole search with the claimed straight line at width 22 (every trial must return a 22-bit partial collision; our 2,304 local trials took 18.01 steps on average against 17.94 for an ideal random function); proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps and tests 22-bit agreement among 2,048 iterates (model 0.3934 per trial). Our own C runs (proof.md Section 7.2) on the program file: pair-coincidence rates on three 32-bit windows (including the distinguished-point bits) among 2^24 images of uniform inputs, of the consecutive starts rho + i, and of chained iterates are within 0.6 percent of the random value (sd 0.55 percent); single-bit input differences show no output bias (max |z| 4.09 over 65,536 cells); the proj trial at scale gives 0.3936 in 262,144 trials. Extrapolated from 22- and 32-bit projections to 256-bit coincidences at 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption, not proved. The linear round 0 leaves five nonlinear rounds; a structural deviation of the collision rate at 256 bits that does not appear in 22- and 32-bit projections is not excluded. If the pair-coincidence rate is (1 - eps) of uniform, the same success costs about 0.5 log2(1/(1 - eps)) more bits (0.0073 for eps = 0.01). Our Python proj-w256 runs gave 859/2,304 = 0.373 against 0.393 (z = -2.0) while the C run at scale gave 0.3936 (z = +0.2).

heuristics.statement: The 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 has a file of 2,192 registers of 256 bits (2,181 used by the straight line, 11 by the search state). A register operand costs nothing beyond the operation that uses it. All transfers are charged as stated: the straight line has no loads or stores, and every load and store of the other code is a charged word operation (proof.md Sections 3.5 and 4). The file's 70,144 bytes are counted as memory (Section 6).
heuristics.scope: The register file of the machine that runs the step program and the search of proof.md Section 4; it affects the time and memory ledgers only, not the success bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: The cost model and the target profile fix no register count; this is a declared machine convention, not a measured property. Executed checks (selftest, the experiments) validate the functional output of the program with this allocation, not the cost of register access.
heuristics.limitations: Not established by the cost model. With fewer registers the same straight line needs loads and stores (Belady eviction, spill.py): 1,024 registers +9,718 per step, score 124.608; 512 registers 124.810; 256 registers +20,763 per step, score 124.966; 64 registers 125.119 (proof.md Section 8).

heuristics.statement: The straight line is native code of the machine, stored at 5 bytes per instruction (3-bit opcode and three 12-bit register numbers), executed directly: each instruction is one primitive operation and control falls through to the next, with no interpreter, so no decode, dispatch or index arithmetic is executed or charged. All other code is charged 32 bytes per instruction, at most 4,096 instructions (proof.md Sections 3.5 and 6).
heuristics.scope: The size of the stored straight line (142,790 bytes with the prefilter) in the memory table and the absence of decode cost in the time ledger; it does not affect the success bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: The cost model and the target profile fix no code encoding; this is a declared machine convention. The executed checks decode the 5-byte encoding in software to validate the program's function; they do not validate native execution or its cost.
heuristics.limitations: Not established by the cost model. At 32 bytes per instruction the straight line alone takes 913,856 bytes; the best parameters found then give a score of about 124.82 (coarse scan, not certified; proof.md Section 8). The 4,096-instruction size of the other code is a declared bound, not a measured size.
